skill.name: latex-posters
skill.description: Create professional research posters in LaTeX using beamerposter, tikzposter, or baposter. The skill helps with conference layouts, academic poster structure, visual hierarchy, figure placement, and print-ready PDF review.
skill.summary: Create conference-ready LaTeX research posters with templates, design guidance, and quality checks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from LaTeX examples, Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and poster-design words such as grid and avoid. The only executable file, scripts/review_poster.sh, runs fixed local PDF inspection commands with quoted file paths. I found no command injection, exfiltration, persistence, or prompt injection intent.

content.value_statement: Research posters are hard to format and proof for print in LaTeX. This skill provides templates, layout guidance, and PDF checks for conference-ready posters.
actual_capabilities: Selects between beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter for different poster styles.
Provides reusable LaTeX poster templates for common academic layouts.
Guides poster structure, typography, color contrast, and visual hierarchy.
Helps integrate figures, tables, equations, citations, logos, and QR codes.
Includes checklists for print readiness, accessibility, and visual review.
Provides a local PDF review script for page size, fonts, file size, and images.
limitations: Requires a working LaTeX environment and the selected poster package.
Does not replace conference poster rules or printer specifications.
AI-generated schematic guidance depends on a separate skill that is not included here.
The review script checks PDF properties but cannot verify scientific accuracy.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Conference Poster
use_cases.description: Turn research notes, figures, and results into a structured poster for a poster session.

use_cases.title: Standardize Lab Posters
use_cases.description: Create reusable templates with consistent branding, section layout, and print settings for a research group.

use_cases.title: Review a Print PDF
use_cases.description: Check poster size, page count, embedded fonts, image presence, and manual review steps before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with basic research details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a LaTeX research poster outline for my project. I need a 36 by 48 inch landscape poster with sections for background, methods, results, and conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Package selection before writing the poster.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter for my academic poster. Recommend one package based on a clean institutional style and several large figures.

prompt_templates.title: Improve the Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my poster layout for readability, visual hierarchy, column balance, figure placement, and accessibility. Suggest specific changes before I compile the PDF.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Print
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare my compiled poster PDF for printing. Check size, fonts, images, file size, QR codes, and the final manual inspection checklist.

output_examples.input: I need an A0 portrait poster for a biology conference with methods, results, and a QR code.
output_examples.output: A recommended tikzposter structure with a clear title area, three-column content plan, visual balance guidance, and print review steps.

output_examples.input: My poster has too much text and the figures feel small.
output: Reduce body text to short bullet points.
Move the main result into the center column.
Use stronger section headers and more white space.

output_examples.input: I have a final PDF and need to check whether it is ready for submission.
output_examples.output: A quality review plan covering page dimensions, one-page output, file size, embedded fonts, image checks, and final proofreading.

best_practices: Start with the conference size requirement before choosing a template.
Use large figures, short text blocks, and consistent alignment across columns.
Run a final PDF review and complete a manual visual inspection before printing.
anti_patterns: Do not fill the poster with long paragraphs or small body text.
Do not rely only on color to explain important results.
Do not submit a PDF without checking size, fonts, images, and QR codes.

faq.question: Which LaTeX poster package should I use?
faq.answer: Use beamerposter for traditional academic style, tikzposter for modern graphics, and baposter for box-based layouts.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete poster?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help draft structure, layout, LaTeX template content, figure placement, and final review steps.

faq.question: Does it compile the poster automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest compilation commands. Actual compilation requires a local LaTeX installation and the needed packages.

faq.question: Can it check my PDF before printing?
faq.answer: Yes. The included script checks page size, page count, file size, fonts, and image information when supporting tools are installed.

faq.question: Does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for contrast, color-blind friendly palettes, readable typography, and clear visual hierarchy.

faq.question: Can it verify my scientific claims?
faq.answer: No. It improves poster communication and formatting, but subject matter accuracy needs expert review.
